analysis.investment_thesis: Pajson Agro fails both Magic Formula pillars: ROE of just 0.60% implies near-zero ROIC, and a P/E of 18.3 (earnings yield ~5.5%) is not cheap enough to compensate. Cashew processing is a low-margin commodity conversion business with no visible moat — this is neither "good" nor "cheap."
key_strengths: Promoter holding healthy at 62.47%, skin in the game
Listed in FMCG-adjacent segment with export optionality
DII holding 7.63% suggests some institutional interest
key_risks: ROE of 0.60% is effectively no return on capital — Magic Formula fails
P/E 18.3 on near-zero profitability implies extreme overvaluation on EV/EBIT
Commodity cashew processing: thin margins, raw material price exposure, no moat
red_flags: ROE 0.60% — capital is being destroyed in real terms vs cost of capital
Incorporated only in 2021 — no 3-year track record of sustained ROIC
Earnings yield likely well below 6% threshold given the weak profitability
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks companies on two axes: how cheap (EBIT/EV) and how good (ROIC). Pajson Agro fails decisively on the "good" axis with ROE of 0.60% — for a non-leveraged commodity processor this implies ROIC in low single digits at best, far below the >20% threshold I look for. A P/E of 18.3 translates to an earnings yield of roughly 5.5%, which is below the 6% floor I consider acceptable even for a mediocre business, let alone a bad one. The combination — low returns AND no valuation cushion — is exactly what the formula is designed to screen OUT.

Cashew kernel processing is a classic low-value-add commodity business: buy raw nuts, shell/grade/pack, sell kernels. Margins are structurally thin, working capital intensive, and exposed to both raw material (African/Vietnamese cashew) and output price swings. A 2021-incorporated entity with ₹374 Cr market cap and sub-1% ROE looks like a post-IPO SME priced on hope, not earnings power. There is nothing in the Magic Formula framework that would justify buying this — the correct action is to pass and deploy capital into names ranking in the top decile on both earnings yield and ROIC.
